![[7ad0p7aw4139rc0ae60cwgygd0]]
> Maybe what Blygger miners earn are "coins" that could be spent promoting content on some kind of Blygger frontpage. That makes it a decentralized editorial system. Maybe there's a sort of Reddit of the thicket, and miners get upvotes or downvotes that they can allocate by burning coins.

I’d definitely keep this sort of thing off-protocol. Ie stay agnostic to it but neither enshrine nor outlaw it.  My suspicion is that with sufficient AI in the mix you don’t need a tokenized mechanism for this kind of thing. You want to create a “Blygger frontpage” (I plan to make blygger.com a reference front page but explicitly establish that there can be no canonical front page).

I’m still getting a sense of how pins should behave. Mostly likely in an IPFS way. So filecoin would be a good reference for any crypto-style tokenization.

I do think we need a natural way to integrate a payment rails into blygger for various sorts of paywall and donation patterns. But again I don’t want to designate one right answer.

I’m still getting a sense of how pins should behave. Mostly likely in an IPFS way. So filecoin would be a good reference for any crypto-style tokenization.

I do think we need a natural way to integrate a payment rails into blygger for various sorts of paywall and donation patterns. But again I don’t want to designate one right answer.
